summary: Focused re-test of the ?token= hardening in GET /api/mod/site/attachments/serve. pytest: 15/16 pass. All requested cases pass. (1) A JWT used as ?token= after POST /api/auth/logout returns 401 with no cookie, for both an outsider (403 before logout, 401 after) and the site user (200 before, 401 after). (2) is_active=False on the seed TEST user gives 401 on the ?token= JWT, and 200 again once the flag is removed. (3) The iteration_297 cases are unchanged: JWT -> 200, cookie only -> 200, token=cookie + cookie -> 200, garbage token + cookie -> 200, a revoked query token + a valid cookie from another session -> 200 via the cookie, no auth -> 401, token=cookie with no cookie -> 401, other org -> 403, bad path or '..' -> 400, missing file -> 404. UI: a real MOD login (localStorage.token='cookie') opens Faults > the seeded fault, and both fault-photo thumbnails load (naturalWidth 40, serve requests return 200, the src has no token). The one failing extra test: the new check reads 'is_active', but user accounts are disabled with 'active' (login, pulse_master_admin revoke), so a user with active:false still gets 200 on ?token=.

minor.issue: The inactive-user check reads viewer.get('is_active') is False. The users collection does not use is_active for disabling accounts. Login (_enforce_account_status in routes/auth.py:482) checks 'active' is False. pulse_master_admin.py:307 revokes users with {'active': False}, and master_admin_users.py:1182 sets 'disabled'. Only 2 users in the DB have is_active at all. Reproduced: TEST user with active:false -> ?token= JWT still returns 200. Suggest: reject if viewer.get('active') is False or viewer.get('is_active') is False or viewer.get('disabled').

This behaviour is app-wide, not new, and is for info. An existing ga_session cookie still works for /api/auth/me and the serve endpoint after the user is set to active:false or disabled:true. Only revocation is checked, so a disabled user keeps access until their token expires.

action_items: In mod_attachment_serve, also treat user.active is False (and disabled is True) as inactive in the ?token= branch. Today only is_active is checked, and user accounts do not use that field.
(Optional, app-wide) Think about checking active/disabled in get_current_user so disabled users lose cookie sessions as well.
critical_code_review_comments: mod_attachment_serve L808: wrong or incomplete field for deactivation (is_active vs active/disabled).
Fallback order is correct: a revoked or inactive query token sets viewer=None and then falls through to the cookie, so a stale ?token= in a link does not break a signed-in user.
is_jwt_revoked honours the effective_at grace window. Logout uses grace 0, so revocation takes effect at once (verified).
